biodiversity_overview.text: 48,862 GBIF occurrence records for 74 tracked species are attributed to Uttarakhand, spanning 1865-2026.
47,558 of these records (97.3%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 28, Magnoliopsida 17, Mammalia 14, Testudines 5, Amphibia 3, Squamata 3, Crocodylia 1, Pinopsida 1, Actinopterygii 1, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 9 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN), Asian Elephant (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian White-eye (11,710), Indian Grey-Hornbill (9,969), Indian Cuckoo (4,328), Indian Pied Starling (4,140), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (3,081).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,891 in 2016 to 283 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 14.65% of Uttarakhand's area (16 areas intersect the state).
8.6% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (4,098 of 47,558); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Spikenard (0.64), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Courser (0.47).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Uttarakhand (equal-weight reference): cell near 28.875N 79.125E (overall rank 14, median rank across weightings 20); cell near 28.875N 79.875E (overall rank 17, median rank across weightings 26); cell near 29.625N 78.375E (overall rank 82, median rank across weightings 90).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 19,699 km2 (35.75% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

226.9 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.15% of the 2000 extent; 0.57% in 2015-2024, rank 18 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2023 (19.97 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.65% of land and population density is 213.4 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
24% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
